newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Azevedo optimistic on Sonae's industrial business.
newsitem.headline: Azevedo optimistic on Sonae's industrial business.

text.p: The chairman of the Sonae Investimentos group, Belmiro de Azevedo, said that he was optimistic about the group's Sonae Industria industrial arm after the restructuring of its wood products business and new investment.
"Last year we presented interesting results and this year they are probably going to be better," he told Reuters during the World Economic Forum here.
"Above all the cash flow in the wood sector is big and permits re-investment. The investments are big, the amortisation of funds is big, but so is the flow of funds," he said.

Following the restructuring of the wood interests, Sonae had probably the most efficient set-up for aglomerates and medium-density fibreboard (MDF) in the Iberian peninsular where it has four production centres -- three in Spain and one in Portugal.
"In Iberia we are leaders in quantity and we have probably the best logistics," he said. "We are close to markets and to raw materials."

Azevedo said that Sonae Industria had no immediate further plans for investment after the recent burst of expansion, which has seen or will see new facilities in Canada, two in Brazil and one in Zimbabwe.
There might still be the need for some consolidation of the wood business in Spain, where there were still too many plants, but the main part of Sonae's reconstruction had been completed, he said.
Azevedo said that the initial idea for the reorganisation of the group's Sonae holding had envisaged a split into three parts.

But it opted for the two-way split because it was faster, he said. Sonae Investimentos has the group's retail and property interests, while Sonae Industria and Pargeste, the services group, are incorporated into Inparsa.
But from a management point of view, Sonae Industria and Pargeste will operate completely independently. Inparsa has 100 percent of Pargeste and 61 percent of Sonae Industria.
Azevedo said that Sonae Investimentos was studying building two more supermarkets in southern Brazil in addition to the two in Florianopolis, in the state of Santa Catarina.
He said the prospects for Brazil were very good and with the Portuguese market virtually saturated as far as his group was concerned, Brazil offered the best possibility of growth.
"It is natural that Brazil comes in our area of expansion," he said.
